n1.text: Can you read a fault or lockout code from the boiler display or control?

r_code.cause: A fault code identifies the safety or condition that locked out the boiler.
fix: Record the code and time before resetting.
Look it up in the Fault codes tab, then confirm in the manufacturer manual (Manuals tab).
Follow the manufacturer's reset procedure. Repeated lockouts mean the cause must be found, not reset away.

n2.text: Which safety circuit opened? (Check status indicators per the boiler manual.)

options.label: Air pressure, flue or condensate switch

fix: Check gas supply and shutoffs, igniter and flame sensor per the manufacturer's procedure.
Gas work follows the manufacturer's procedure and local code.
Check system pressure, water level or low-water cut-off, and look for leaks.
Check pump operation and flow switch.
Do not bypass the low-water cut-off or flow switch.
If the boiler is hot and low on water, let it cool before adding water.
Allow the boiler to cool before resetting.
Check flow, supply sensor accuracy and setpoints.
Do not raise or bypass the limit.

r_air.cause: Air pressure, flue or condensate switch is open.
fix: Check vent and intake for blockage, the condensate drain and trap, and the switch tubing per the manual.

r_unknown.cause: The tripped safety cannot be identified from outside.
fix: Check the boiler manual's status indicator or diagnostics section (Manuals tab: search lockout).
Check the control for stored fault history.
Contact the manufacturer support line if the cause is still unclear.
